## D569 — OWNER: blind-DM experiment, luna (high, then medium, then low) vs sol high with screenshot only and no engine legal/recommended moves (2026-09-06 22:54)

Owner (verbatim): "Cue up another experiment where we try to get Luna
(high first, then medium after high is maxed out, then low lastly) to
perform as well as sol high where both are given a screenshot but no
output of legal or recommended moves from the engine. I want to see how
good we can get the ai dm to perform given only the rules of the game,
general tips, all of the visual representations of tabletop state, and
instructions on how to interpret the screenshot.

My hope is that we can make the ai dm better at knowing when to
override the engine top recommendation. I hope that The better it can
independently understand how to run the game like a human would, the
more often it will improve upon performance of just following the
engine advice and getting cheesed out like the bg3 algorithm does.

You will need the judges panel to rate the performance of different
models."

Supervisor reading, recorded so it can be corrected: a "blind" DM mode
in which the turn context carries the rules KB, general tactics tips,
the DM board screenshot(s) with the interpretation primer, the
initiative timeline and creature names/HP bands as the board shows
them, and NOTHING derived from the option engine: no offered options,
no intel, no adverts, no suggested plan, no consequence cards. The
model states its intent for each monster in a small typed grammar
(actor by name, action kind and named target or destination cell using
the board's coordinate gutter), and the engine resolves that intent
deterministically to a legal offered option or rejects it with a typed
code. Standing-rule conflict, named: "the model may never emit
coordinates, paths, dice, DCs, damage or reducer commands". Under D569
the model must name destinations somehow; the reading is that
coordinates as board labels are the owner's intended input in this
mode (the gutter exists for it), while dice, DCs, damage and reducer
commands stay forbidden and the engine remains the sole authority over
legality and resolution (a rejected intent never acts). If the owner
wants destinations expressed only relatively ("adjacent to the wizard",
"behind the pillar"), say so and the grammar shrinks. Order of arms:
luna high blind vs sol high blind (and sol high with engine advice as
the ceiling reference), judged by the standing panel on the hard and
brutal bases; luna medium once luna high is maxed; luna low last. The
override study (blind judgement vs engine top recommendation) follows
once blind play is measured. Codex writes the plan; supervisor
critiques before any implementation.

## D569 plan round 1 received; supervisor critique sent as round 2 (2026-09-06 23:17)

Codex plan (587 lines, .tmp-plans/2026-09-06-blind-dm-no-engine-advice.md,
copied to the main repo): blind DM mode with an exact turn-context
allowlist (names, badges, sides, HP bands, initiative, image roles,
primer version), closed MCP tool profile, D569 CC-BY KB bundle shared by
blind and advice arms, typed intent grammar with the gutter label as the
only coordinate form, private deterministic resolver over
availableEngineActorOptions, closed rejection enum, code-only vs
labelled minimal-hint repair arms, byte-level ingress leak audit,
state-only screenshot capture, packet compatibility via the existing
resolutionSummary, arms and cohorts, -0.20 noninferiority with
seed-clustered CI, second seed family as fluke guard, "maxed" = two
consecutive no-gain tuning rounds, override study recorded now as
answer-key-only fields, five increments with tests/mutants/markers.
Two catches by codex that the record did not have: snapshot mode passes
the engine's offered movement paths into the capture even with the UI
toggle off (a blind screenshot would carry advice in pixels), and the
DM timeline's next-event preview can print an exact save DC.

Supervisor critique (round 2, brief blind-dm-plan-r2.md): (1)
structural: the ambiguity rule rejects any attack without a destination
when a moving variant exists and any relative phrase with two candidate
cells, so refusal rate would dominate the panel; required: no
destination = hold, relative phrases resolve by a documented geometric
convention printed in the primer, strict rejection only for genuine
semantic ambiguity; (2) area spells unreachable (no area anchor in the
grammar; entangle is the brutal room-1 opener); (3) attempts default 3
under the 240 s wall; (4) report refusals-as-zero and executed-only
plus refusal rate with CI; (5) tips authorship clean-room CC-BY, never
from the private research tree; (6) split increment 1; (7) confirm the
initiative hp_band is exactly the board's knowledge-policy band; (8)
capture and first-token latency; (9) ceiling arm comparability with
the standing sol-high baseline; (10) who generates and verifies the
second seed family. Session resumed (same id confirmed).

## D576.2 — OWNER: cover is not linked to passability; looked up in the SRD and community rulings (2026-09-07 13:30)

Owner (verbatim): "Look up in the srd and what the community rulings
are. I don't think cover is necessary linked to pass ability"

Lookup: SRD 5.2.1 (docs/srd/full/srd-5.2.1.txt lines 925-954) defines
cover by how much of the target an object or creature covers and says
nothing about movement; the Difficult Terrain rule (lines 872-883)
names "low furniture, rubble, undergrowth, steep stairs" as examples,
the same objects that grant half cover; another creature's space is
difficult terrain and creatures grant half cover. Community reading
(2014 text: "a low wall, a large piece of furniture, a narrow tree
trunk, or a creature" as half cover; jumping "a hedge or low wall" with
an Athletics check at the GM's option): low cover is crossable at a
cost, tall solid things are not, and cover degree is independent of
passability. No official ruling links the two.

Ruling as applied to D576 (supersedes the plan's default): each terrain
feature carries two typed dimensions, cover tier (none, half,
three_quarters, total) and passability (open, difficult, blocked), with
the consistency rules total => blocked and blocked-sight => total. Walls
(existing blocked cells) are total + blocked + no sight; generated low
cover (barricades, crates, low walls) is half + difficult; arrow slits
and portcullises are three_quarters + blocked; living creatures give
half cover and their space is difficult terrain as the SRD says. The
map draws both cues per feature (tier mark and a crossable mark),
the legend names both, and the query tool reports both. Increment 1a
dispatched with this ruling.

CORRECTION OF MY OWN FINDING, at full length because it is against my
own work. I committed 73c4b2ba describing this as a defect in codex's
implementation, saying the refusal guard "needs the UPPER bound". Astra,
now the decider, checked the approved plan and found line 407 requires
"neither basis has a CI-excluding increase in refused/execution-failure
rate", and an increase is CI-excluding exactly when the interval's lower
bound is above zero. I verified that line myself. So codex implemented
the approved plan CORRECTLY and my commit message misattributes the
fault. The weakness is in the plan's own success rule, which I reviewed
and approved. What the mutant really proved is that the rule is
untested, not that the code is wrong. The follow-up commit carries the
correct framing.

D578.1 (decider ruling, pre-results, ACCEPTED): the refusal clause is
STRENGTHENED to require the UPPER bound at or below its own new named
margin D569_REFUSAL_RISK_MARGIN = 0.00, never the offense margin.
Missing, non-finite or reversed intervals can never qualify. Astra's
point stands that zero tolerance is demanding and a failed gate means
noninferiority was not established rather than inferiority proved.
Pinning table given to the lane verbatim: [-0.10,-0.01], [-0.10,0.00]
and [0.00,0.00] pass; [-0.10,0.01], [0.00,0.01] and [0.01,0.10] fail;
a negative mean with a positive upper bound fails; offense lower bound
exactly -0.20 fails; and an end-to-end two-cluster fixture whose paired
refusal differences are 0 and 1 has the exact bootstrap distribution
0, 0.5, 1 at one quarter, one half, one quarter, so offense passes and
refusal fails, while swapping the arms gives [-1,0] and passes. Seven
mutants required: lower-for-upper, mean-for-interval, reversed sign,
reversed inequality, strict less-than, omitted guard, OR for AND.

D578.2 (decider ruling, ACCEPTED): the Fable PLAYER arm is dropped from
this registration rather than substituted or waited on, because

also corrected my premise here: substituting itself would NOT have made

## D641 — OWNER (2026-09-17 18:48): "I think we need to model that a wall is solid across cells. It is not just a series of cells. Look for how others have handled this." — research done by the supervisor; question put back to the owner
PROBED BY ME on 807d2e3c (traceTerrainLine, 6x6 board): (1) two blockers touching only at a corner, (2,1)&(1,2), observer (0,0) → target (3,3) through the shared vertex: tier half, blocksSight FALSE — the diagonal crack lets sight through; (2) solid 2x2 block: total, TRUE; (3) wall column with the ray along its face-line between two blockers (the D635 seam): half, TRUE; (4) a ray grazing one blocker's corner: none, FALSE. So today's tracer = closed cells whose interiors block + the D635 shared-EDGE rule; shared CORNERS of diagonally touching blockers are still open.
HOW OTHERS DO IT (sources in the reply): D&D 2014 DMG corner trace — lines from a corner to the target's corners; whether a line that merely TOUCHES an obstacle counts is explicitly the DM's call (the SRD 5.2.1 only defines cover degrees by "covers at least half / three-quarters / the whole target"); Gloomhaven — corner-to-corner lines, and "the line cannot touch or cross a wall at any point; touching the very edge of a wall still means no LOS" (walls are closed sets; touching = blocked); Foundry VTT / Roll20 — walls are SEGMENTS with endpoints (thin walls), not cells, so no cell seams exist and a long wall is one solid segment by construction; roguelikes (Red Blob "thin wall FOV", Adam Milazzo's survey, Albert Ford's symmetric shadowcasting, RogueBasin comparative study) — "thick walls" (blocking cells) vs "thin walls" (blocking edges) is the standard framing, and diagonal-gap peeking between corner-touching blockers is a known nuisance that implementations bevel or seal; Debenham & Solis-Oba, "New Algorithms for Computing Field of Vision over 2D Grids" (arXiv 2101.11002) — "adjacent vision blocking cells are first grouped together into rectilinear regions, then split into a minimal number of rectangles", and their Figure 5 is exactly our seam: two adjacent rectangles let a ray slip along the shared side, which they fix by extending one rectangle to overlap the other so the union is solid.
PROPOSAL (to the owner, one question): adopt a SOLID-WALL model — the wall is the union of sight-blocking cells as closed rectilinear regions; a ray is blocked iff it passes through the union's interior, which includes (a) any blocking cell's interior, (b) an edge shared by two blockers (D635, already in), and (c) a vertex shared by two diagonally touching blockers (seal the crack; NOT in today). Grazing an OUTER face or a single blocker's corner stays open (DMG-consistent, today's behaviour). Implementation: step 1 a local vertex rule beside firstSharedEdgeBlockingCell in cover.ts with witnesses for all four probe cases (small, rules-visible, needs its own D-ruling and astra review; lands with VIS-FIELD); step 2 the precomputed rectilinear-region/rectangle representation keyed by the blocking topology (the paper's approach) as the VIS-FIELD-PERF batch (also perf fix #3 in D635.53). Question 5 stays: regenerate the cohorts under the solid-wall geometry (A1).

# Investigation result

Option A has a real, existing precedent—fresh namespace, fresh directory, frozen ledger evidence, two independent generations, semantic membership checks before hashes, then a versioned manifest—but it is not an automated “regenerate family” facility. The D569 second family was a new independent evaluation cohort, not a regenerated version of the first family.

A clean Option A should therefore create new cohorts and new manifest identities while preserving all existing fixture bytes, manifests, replay rows, and approved-main evidence. Because the current D569 second-family validator also detects the removed `foggedCells` field, a complete replacement needs 40 new fixtures, not merely the 30 brutal fixtures: ten new hard second-family fixtures are needed to make the v2 second-family manifest byte-regenerable without rewriting history.

## 1. Existing D569 regeneration and versioning machinery

### What the two regeneration codes mean

In [tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:464):

- `first_regeneration` means generation run 1 must equal the committed fixture bytes exactly.
- `independent_regeneration` means generation run 2 must equal both run 1 and the committed fixture bytes.
- Both runs call `generateRoom(seed, { difficulty })`, serialize with canonical JSON, and append one newline at lines 483–489.
- The `generation` argument is intentionally ignored by the canonical implementation; it exists so tests can prove that the validator really calls and compares a second execution.

Thus “independent regeneration” means a second deterministic build execution, not a later cohort version.

The second-family test explicitly kills a validator that fails to compare generation 2 at [tests/unit/tools/d569-second-family-manifest.test.ts:179](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tests/unit/tools/d569-second-family-manifest.test.ts:179).

### What the second family actually was

The D569 second family was a fluke-guard evaluation cohort:

- Hard: `5118001–5118010`
- Brutal: `6207001–6207010`
- Directories: `arena-basis-hard-2` and `arena-basis-brutal-2`

The original proposal used `6204001–6204010`, but that was rejected because 6204 was already the D466 override/protocol namespace. Main’s decision record then selected 6207 and required any membership failure to stop generation, with no hand edits or override entries: [decisions.md:14690](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-multiclass-spells-static/.claude/decisions.md:14690).

That is the sanctioned precedent for a new family:

1. Predeclare unused seed ranges.
2. Record the namespace audit verbatim.
3. Generate into a new directory.
4. Prove structural and behavioral membership from decoded state.
5. Generate twice and compare bytes.
6. Pin hashes only after those proofs.
7. Nest the resulting manifest hash in the experiment manifest.

It is not a migration path for modifying the old family in place.

### What the ledger test compares

The ledger entry is frozen at [tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:24](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:24) and in [tests/fixtures/d569-second-family-manifest.json:8](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tests/fixtures/d569-second-family-manifest.json:8). It states:

- `5118xxx` and `6207xxx` had no occurrence in decisions, fixtures, or tools as of 2026-09-07.
- `5117xxx`, `6203xxx`, `6204xxx`, `6206xxx`, and `6208xxx` were already used.

The validator checks:

- Exact ledger text, not the result of a fresh repository grep.
- Exact hard and brutal contiguous seed arrays.
- Exact cohort directories and paths.
- No overlap with every listed used namespace.
- No D466 per-seed override.
- Fixture SHA-256.
- Seed and state membership.
- Two byte-identical regenerations.

Those checks are at [tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:359](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts:359) through line 476. The corresponding ledger test is [tests/unit/tools/d569-second-family-manifest.test.ts:77](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tests/unit/tools/d569-second-family-manifest.test.ts:77).

A new version must therefore contain a new dated ledger statement. Reusing or editing the old sentence would falsify historical evidence.

### What `second_family_first_regeneration` validates

The outer experiment validator reads the nested second-family manifest, validates it, and prefixes every inner violation with `second_family_` at [tools/d569-blind-experiment.ts:602](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tools/d569-blind-experiment.ts:602). Consequently:

`second_family_first_regeneration`

means “the current generator’s first canonical rebuild differs from a fixture named by the nested second-family manifest.”

It does not mean “the first family was regenerated.”

The current 47 inner violations decompose as:

- 20 second-family fixtures × two byte-regeneration failures = 40. The historical bytes contain the now-removed `foggedCells` state field.
- Seven brutal-2 fixtures fail current `brutal_productivity` under the seam rule = 7.
- Total = 47.

## 3. Concrete Option A batch

### Proposed fresh namespaces

These are provisional until the implementation preflight proves both absence and membership:

| Purpose | Proposed range | Directory |
|---|---:|---|
| Primary brutal v2 | 6209001–6209010 | `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-brutal-v2` |
| Brutal-b v2 | 6210001–6210010 | `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-brutal-b-v2` |
| D569 second brutal v2 | 6211001–6211010 | `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-brutal-2-v2` |
| D569 second hard v2 | 5120001–5120010 | `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-hard-3` |

An exact tracked-file grep found zero explicit uses of all four ranges. `5119xxx` is unsuitable: seed 5119001 already appears twice in `tests/unit/tools/ai-dm-arena.test.ts`.

The hard addition is necessary because all ten existing hard-2 fixtures fail both current byte-regeneration checks after the fog-field removal. Reusing them in v2 would leave 20 of the current 47 manifest violations.

### Generation

For each range, use the existing tool with no terrain override:

```sh
node_modules/.bin/vite-node tools/generate-arena-basis.ts -- \
  --difficulty brutal --seed 6209001 --rooms 10 \
  --out tests/fixtures/arena-basis-brutal-v2
```

Repeat for 6210001 and 6211001; use `--difficulty hard --seed 5120001` for the new hard cohort.

Before committing fixtures:

1. Generate each cohort into two different temporary directories.
2. `diff -rq` the two outputs.
3. Decode every room and run integrity plus difficulty membership checks.
4. For brutal rooms, prove every living monster has a productive, resolvable first-turn option under the current offer environment.
5. Confirm every relevant opposing ray considered “open” has both `tier === 'none'` and `blocksSight === false`; that predicate is now explicit at [src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1227](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/src/vtt/room-generator.ts:1227).
6. Reject the entire proposed range if any room fails; do not edit a room or add an override.

The D466 6204 mechanism is not a regeneration facility. Its three replacements—6204004, 6204006, and 6204009—are historical typed-roster corrections. The new manifest must retain the `d466GeneratedRoomOverride(seed) === null` guard. If a candidate needs a D466-style replacement, choose another fresh namespace.

### Versioning and pins

Create:

- `d569-second-family-manifest-v2.json`
  - New hard and brutal ranges.
  - New exact ledger evidence.
  - Version `d569-second-family-manifest-v2`.
  - Two independent regenerations.
- `d569-blind-experiment-manifest-v6.json`
  - Primary hard may remain 5117.
  - Primary brutal becomes 6209.
  - Nested second-family reference becomes v2 with its new hash.
  - Preserve v5 unchanged.

Update schemas and constants in:

- `tools/d569-second-family-manifest.ts`
- `tools/d569-blind-experiment.ts`

Split the runtime tests so v5 remains historical and v6 is the active executable manifest. In particular, do not silently make a file named `d569-v5.test.ts` execute v6.

New cryptographic pins:

- 10 primary brutal fixture hashes.
- 10 brutal-b fixture hashes.
- 10 second-family brutal hashes.
- 10 second-family hard hashes.
- One second-family manifest hash.
- One outer experiment manifest hash.
- Total: 42 distinct new SHA-256 values, though some are repeated in test tables.

D569 counts do not change:

- 480 core cells per family.
- 660 primary cells with hint arms.
- 240 core cells affected by each brutal half.
- 330 primary brutal cells when its hint arms are included.

All session keys, visual-source hashes, and state hashes must become v6 identities; v5 and v6 result rows must not be pooled as if they were the same experiment.

### Demonstrate, then normalize

Before inserting any hash:

- Demonstrate unused namespaces with a recorded exact grep.
- Demonstrate no D466 override.
- Demonstrate decoded integrity, budget, caster, terrain, and productivity properties.
- Demonstrate actual seam-clear sight for the productive offers.
- Demonstrate generation A equals generation B.
- Add negative witnesses:
  - a blocked-sight ray with physical tier `none` must fail the open-ray condition;
  - one deliberately nonproductive monster must fail membership;
  - changing only generation 2 must yield `independent_regeneration`;
  - a matching hash must not excuse failed state membership.

Only then compute fixture hashes independently, insert them into manifests, and pin the two manifest hashes. A test access shim that merely returns the committed fixture as its “regeneration” does not constitute this proof; at least one active v6 test must call the real generator.

### Active route changes versus historical consumers

Add versioned routes rather than retargeting historical names:

- `brutal-v2` and `brutal-b-v2` arena basis labels, or require an explicit `--basis-dir` for v2. The former is safer operationally because it prevents accidental fallback to the old default paths.
- Add `brutal-10-v2` and `brutal-10-b-v2` rerun protocols.
- Add new families to `los-cover-era-audit.ts` and active context reports.
- Keep `brutal-10`, `brutal-10-b`, and current arena basis defaults available for historical replay.

Renderer, snapshot, hidden-option, challenge, and conversation tests that use a particular old seed as a scene should remain on that seed. They are not active-cohort selectors.

### Estimated size

Minimal cohort and D569 work:

- 40 new room fixtures.
- 2 new manifests.
- Approximately 14 source/test modifications.
- About 56 touched or added paths.

Full active-route reconciliation, including arena/rerun/audit wiring and the three behavior tests:

- 40 fixture files.
- 2 manifest files.
- Approximately 20–24 source and test files.
- Approximately 62–66 paths total.

Existing family density implies about 865 KB of new fixture JSON, before manifest and test changes.

Principal risks:

- Choosing seeds because the generated output happens to pass and then using the same implementation to certify its own output.
- Allowing D466 overrides or hand edits to conceal a failed candidate.
- Replacing v5/v1 bytes rather than adding v6/v2.
- Mixing old and new experiment rows despite changed state hashes.
- Updating approved-main or legacy replay artifacts.
- Letting the `seed - 6203000` ordinal assumption in `d569-v5.test.ts` survive into v6.
- Repinning behavioral output without an independent geometry derivation or negative witness.

## 4. Three hard-family behavior pins

### Composite turn proposals: hand-derived re-pin

[composite-turn-proposals.test.ts:153](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tests/unit/vtt/composite-turn-proposals.test.ts:153) can be re-pinned without changing its scene.

The scout is at `(13,3)`. The three targets are fighter `(1,2)`, cleric `(2,4)`, and wizard `(1,6)`. Under the seam rule:

- Fighter and cleric have physically non-total rays, but those rays are optically blocked along paired blocking-cell edges.
- Wizard is physically total.
- The legal projected labels are therefore `Dodge` and `End Turn`, not the three Longbow targets.

That is hand-derivable from the four corner rays and remains faithful to the test’s real subject: projection of fresh legal options. The new expectation should include the exact defensive labels and a negative assertion that no Longbow label is exposed.

### Room-8 movement: hand-derived re-pin

[engine-opportunity-movement-intel.test.ts:71](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tests/unit/vtt/engine-opportunity-movement-intel.test.ts:71) also needs no scene change.

The exact new proposal outcomes are derivable from the frozen positions and legal option inventory:

- Monster 1 at `(22,1)`: zero-foot Dodge.
- Monster 2 at `(21,1)`: zero-foot Dodge.
- Monster 4 at `(21,3)`: zero-foot Dodge.
- Monster 5 at `(22,5)`: retains the existing 55-foot Dash to `(12,6)`.

The test still proves its named invariant: the old four-actor zero-foot Dash plan is not repeated. Its current comment claiming all four Dashes are productive must be replaced.

### Speculative planning: scene change required

[speculative-planning.test.ts:543](/home/vagrant/PhpstormProjects/dnd-wt-seam-verify/tests/unit/vtt/speculative-planning.test.ts:543) cannot legitimately be normalized to an empty menu.

For seed 5117001, monster 1 retains productive choices, but monster 2 has only `Dodge` and `End Turn`; the resulting scenario menu is empty. Changing the expectation to zero would remove the test’s subject—forming and ranking a nonempty bounded volatility menu.

Use a small hand-authored scene with:

- Two baseline monster proposals.
- Explicit canonical movement radii.
- At least one player dependency influencing a proposal.
- Independently calculated `volatilityScore = referencedProposalCount × summedMovementRadiusFeet`.
- Exact rank order and the eight-entry cap.
- A seam-blocking mutation that removes the relevant dependency and changes or empties the menu.

Selecting the first generated hard seed that happens to yield a nonempty menu would be another self-generated expectation and should be avoided.

## 5. Alternatives

### Option B: amend the productivity contract

This would relax or replace `everyMonsterProductive` in `brutalRoomMembershipViolations`, the 6203 generator test, the brutal-b membership suite, and the D569 second-family validator. It is roughly a 6–10 file change with no new brutal fixtures, but it does not by itself cure the 40 current regeneration failures caused by the removed fog field; the historical regeneration comparison would still need a version-aware projection or manifest change. It also leaves the speculative-planning scene invalid and weakens the reason these cohorts were selected: brutal-b currently has 41 of 42 monsters without attack offers under the seam-era measurement. Any amended threshold would need to be preregistered and mutation-tested rather than chosen to fit the current failures.

### Option C: revisit the seam rule

This would change the line tracer so a corner ray running along an edge shared by two blocking cells is not optically blocked. The causal probe says this restores all three hard-family behavioral tests and substantially restores offer counts: hard + original brutal + brutal-b rise from 214 to 451 offers when the seam behavior is disabled; brutal-2 rises from 58 to 96. It avoids the 30 new brutal fixtures, but still does not repair the 40 D569 byte-regeneration violations caused by the fog-field removal. It also reverses D635’s optical ruling and requires a wider revalidation of cover, sight, visibility fields, offer/execution agreement, and browser projections—likely 10–20 affected source/test files plus the full landing gates. Its semantic blast radius is greater than Option A’s versioned data cost.

   204	function executableControlCaster(room: GeneratedRoom): boolean {
   205	  return room.spec.monsterRoster.some((entry) => {
   206	    const row = STARTER_MONSTER_ROSTER.find((candidate) => candidate.id === entry.statblockId);

   208	    return actions?.kind === 'present' && actions.value.some((action) =>
   209	      action.kind === 'spellcasting' && action.execution?.kind !== 'absent' &&
   210	      action.spells.some((spell) => {
   211	        const definition = spell.manifestStatus === 'implemented' ? spellDefinition(spell.id) : undefined;
   212	        return definition?.operation.kind === 'persistent_area' &&
   213	          definition.operation.hooks.some((hook) => hook.effect.kind === 'save_gated') &&
   214	          definition.operation.hooks.some((hook) =>
   215	            hook.effect.kind === 'automatic' && hook.effect.payload.kind === 'effect' &&
   216	            hook.effect.payload.payload.kind === 'movement_modifier');
   217	      }));
   218	  });
   219	}

   272	function everyMonsterProductive(room: GeneratedRoom): boolean {
   273	  const planningState = freshMonsterPlanningState(room.encounter.state);
   274	  return planningState.combatants
   275	    .filter((combatant) => combatant.profile.kind === 'monster')
   276	    .every((monster) => availableEngineActorOptions(planningState, monster.profile.id, OFFER_ENVIRONMENT)

   280	          resolution.mechanics.actionSlots.some((slot) =>
   281	            slot.kind === 'attack' || slot.kind === 'saving_throw' || slot.kind === 'cast_spell' ||
   282	            slot.kind === 'use_world_object'));
   283	      }));

   397	      const expectedSeed = expectedSeeds[index];
   398	      addViolation(
   399	        violations,
   400	        !seenSeeds.has(fixture.seed),
   401	        'duplicate_seed',
   402	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} appears more than once`,
   403	      );
   404	      seenSeeds.add(fixture.seed);
   405	      for (const namespace of manifest.usedSeedNamespaces) {
   406	        addViolation(
   407	          violations,
   408	          fixture.seed < namespace.start || fixture.seed > namespace.end,
   409	          'seed_overlap',
   410	          `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} overlaps used namespace ${namespace.label}`,
   411	        );
   412	      }
   413	      addViolation(
   414	        violations,
   415	        d466GeneratedRoomOverride(fixture.seed) === null,
   416	        'generator_override',
   417	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} is subject to a generator override`,
   418	      );
   419	      if (expectedSeed === undefined || fixture.seed !== expectedSeed) continue;
   420	
   421	      const expectedPath = `${cohort.directory}/seed-${String(fixture.seed)}.json`;
   422	      addViolation(
   423	        violations,
   424	        fixture.path === expectedPath,
   425	        'fixture_path',
   426	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} has a non-canonical fixture path`,
   427	      );
   428	      let fixtureBytes: string;
   429	      try {
   430	        fixtureBytes = access.readFixture(fixture.path);
   431	      } catch (error) {
   432	        violations.push({
   433	          code: 'fixture_missing',
   434	          message: `cannot read ${fixture.path}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
   435	        });
   436	        continue;
   437	      }
   438	      addViolation(
   439	        violations,
   440	        sha256(fixtureBytes) === fixture.sha256,
   441	        'fixture_hash',
   442	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} fixture hash changed`,
   443	      );
   444	
   445	      try {
   446	        const room = JSON.parse(fixtureBytes) as GeneratedRoom;
   447	        addViolation(
   448	          violations,
   449	          room.spec.seed === fixture.seed,
   450	          'fixture_seed',
   451	          `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} fixture contains a different seed`,
   452	        );
   453	        violations.push(...generatedRoomIntegrityViolations(room, fixtureBytes));
   454	        violations.push(...(difficulty === 'hard'
   455	          ? hardRoomMembershipViolations(room)
   456	          : brutalRoomMembershipViolations(room)));
   457	      } catch (error) {
   458	        violations.push({
   459	          code: 'fixture_parse',
   460	          message: `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} fixture is invalid JSON: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
   461	        });
   462	      }
   463	
   464	      const firstGeneration = access.regenerate(fixture.seed, difficulty, 1);
   465	      const secondGeneration = access.regenerate(fixture.seed, difficulty, 2);
   466	      addViolation(
   467	        violations,
   468	        firstGeneration === fixtureBytes,
   469	        'first_regeneration',
   470	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} first canonical regeneration differs from the fixture`,
   471	      );
   472	      addViolation(
   473	        violations,
   474	        secondGeneration === firstGeneration && secondGeneration === fixtureBytes,
   475	        'independent_regeneration',
   476	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} independent canonical regeneration differs`,
   477	      );
   478	    }
   479	  }
   480	  return violations;
   481	}

   416	export type D569ExperimentFamily = 'primary' | 'second';

   418	export interface D569ExperimentValidationAccess {

   420	  readonly secondFamilyAccess: D569SecondFamilyValidationAccess;

   428	function addViolation(
   429	  violations: D569ExperimentViolation[],
   430	  condition: boolean,
   431	  code: string,
   432	  message: string,
   433	): void {
   434	  if (!condition) violations.push({ code, message });

   437	function canonicalEqual(left: unknown, right: unknown): boolean {
   438	  return canonicalJson(left) === canonicalJson(right);

   453	] as const);
   454	const REQUIRED_ANSWER_KEY_FIELDS = Object.freeze([
   455	  'selectedOfferedId', 'catalogDigest', 'engineTopId', 'engineTopRank',
   456	  'engineTopPolicyVersion', 'engineTopResolutionDigest', 'blindDiffersFromEngineTop',
   457	  'differenceClass', 'blindCounterfactualDigest', 'engineTopCounterfactualDigest',
   458	] as const);
   459	export const REQUIRED_REPAIR_COMPARISONS = Object.freeze([
   460	  {
   461	    id: 'gpt-5.6-luna-code-only-vs-minhint',
   462	    codeOnlyArm: 'gpt-5.6-luna-blind',
   463	    minimalHintArm: 'gpt-5.6-luna-blind-minhint',
   464	    reportLabel: 'advice-assisted' as const,

   466	  {
   467	    id: 'gpt-5.6-sol-code-only-vs-minhint',
   468	    codeOnlyArm: 'gpt-5.6-sol-blind',
   469	    minimalHintArm: 'gpt-5.6-sol-blind-minhint',
   470	    reportLabel: 'advice-assisted' as const,
   471	  },
   472	  {
   473	    id: 'gpt-6-astra-code-only-vs-minhint',
   474	    codeOnlyArm: 'gpt-6-astra-blind',
   475	    minimalHintArm: 'gpt-6-astra-blind-minhint',
   476	    reportLabel: 'advice-assisted' as const,

   480	function kbComponentKey(path: string): string {
   481	  const filename = path.slice(path.lastIndexOf('/') + 1, -3);
   482	  return filename === 'ai-dm-core' ? 'root' : filename;
   483	}

   485	/** Exact, model-free validation of the preregistration and all frozen inputs. */
   486	export function validateD569ExperimentManifest(
   487	  input: unknown,
   488	  access: D569ExperimentValidationAccess,
   489	): readonly D569ExperimentViolation[] {
   490	  const decoded = d569ExperimentManifestSchema.safeParse(input);
   491	  if (!decoded.success) return [{ code: 'manifest_shape', message: decoded.error.message }];
   492	  const manifest = decoded.data;
   493	  const violations: D569ExperimentViolation[] = [];
   494	
   495	  addViolation(violations, canonicalEqual(manifest.coreArms, D569_CORE_ARM_IDENTITIES),
   496	    'core_arm_set', 'manifest must contain the exact eight active model/mode arms');
   497	  addViolation(violations, canonicalEqual(manifest.hintArms, D569_HINT_ARM_IDENTITIES),
   498	    'hint_arm_set', 'manifest must contain the three preregistered hint diagnostics');
   499	  addViolation(violations, canonicalEqual(manifest.analysisComparisons, D569_ANALYSIS_COMPARISONS),
   500	    'analysis_comparison_set', 'manifest must contain the amended active and advice-ceiling comparisons');
   501	  addViolation(violations,
   502	    canonicalEqual(manifest.judgePanel.scoringSeats, D569_SCORING_PANEL_IDENTITIES),
   503	    'judge_panel', 'judge panel must contain the exact preregistered Fable, Astra, and Sol scoring seats');
   504	  addViolation(violations,
   505	    canonicalEqual(manifest.judgePanel.advisoryNotesStage.source, D569_ADVISORY_NOTES_SOURCE),
   506	    'advisory_notes_source', 'advisory notes must come only from the preregistered Opus 4.8 source');
   507	  addViolation(violations, canonicalEqual(manifest.repairComparisons, REQUIRED_REPAIR_COMPARISONS),
   508	    'repair_comparison_set', 'manifest must contain all three advice-assisted repair comparisons');
   509	  addViolation(violations,
   510	    canonicalEqual(manifest.adviceCeiling.rendererProfile, DEFAULT_RENDERER_PROFILE),
   511	    'advice_renderer', 'advice ceiling must use the standing default renderer');
   512	  addViolation(violations,
   513	    manifest.adviceCeiling.commonKbHash === manifest.sharedKb.combinedStartupHash,
   514	    'advice_kb', 'advice ceiling must use the common D570 KB/tips bytes');
   515	  addViolation(violations, canonicalEqual(manifest.sealedOverride.blindSealFields, REQUIRED_BLIND_SEAL_FIELDS),
   516	    'override_blind_seal_fields', 'sealed override blind fields changed');
   517	  addViolation(violations,
   518	    canonicalEqual(manifest.sealedOverride.answerKeyOnlyFields, REQUIRED_ANSWER_KEY_FIELDS),
   519	    'override_answer_key_fields', 'sealed override answer-key fields changed');
   520	
   521	  const armsById = new Map(
   522	    [...manifest.coreArms, ...manifest.hintArms].map((arm) => [arm.id, arm] as const),
   523	  );
   524	  for (const comparison of manifest.analysisComparisons) {
   525	    const left = armsById.get(comparison.leftArm);
   526	    const right = armsById.get(comparison.rightArm);
   527	    addViolation(violations, left !== undefined && right !== undefined,
   528	      'dangling_comparison_arm', `comparison ${comparison.id} references an inactive arm`);
   529	    if (left === undefined || right === undefined) continue;
   530	    const expectedSeats = ALL_SCORING_SEAT_IDS;
   531	    const registeredSeats = manifest.judgePanel.scoringSeats.filter((seat) =>
   532	      comparison.eligibleJudgeSeats.includes(seat.id));
   533	    addViolation(violations, canonicalEqual(comparison.eligibleJudgeSeats, expectedSeats),
   534	      'judge_eligibility', `comparison ${comparison.id} must use all three registered judge seats`);
   535	    addViolation(violations, expectedSeats.length >= manifest.judgePanel.minimumConsensusSeats &&
   536	      registeredSeats.length >= manifest.judgePanel.minimumConsensusSeats,
   537	      'judge_consensus', `comparison ${comparison.id} has fewer than three eligible judge seats`);
   538	  }
   539	
   540	  const componentKeys = D569_AI_DM_KB_COMPONENT_PATHS.map(kbComponentKey);
   541	  addViolation(violations,
   542	    canonicalEqual(Object.keys(manifest.sharedKb.componentHashes).sort(), [...componentKeys].sort()),
   543	    'kb_component_set', 'shared KB component set changed');
   544	  const componentBytes: string[] = [];
   545	  for (const path of D569_AI_DM_KB_COMPONENT_PATHS) {
   546	    const key = kbComponentKey(path);
   547	    try {
   548	      const bytes = access.readText(path);
   549	      componentBytes.push(bytes);
   550	      addViolation(violations, manifest.sharedKb.componentHashes[key] === sha256(bytes),
   551	        'kb_component_hash', `shared KB component ${path} changed`);
   552	    } catch (error) {
   553	      violations.push({
   554	        code: 'kb_component_missing',
   555	        message: `${path}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
   556	      });
   557	    }
   558	  }
   559	  addViolation(violations,
   560	    componentBytes.length === D569_AI_DM_KB_COMPONENT_PATHS.length &&
   561	      manifest.sharedKb.combinedStartupHash === sha256(componentBytes.join('\n\n')),
   562	  'kb_startup_hash', 'shared D570 startup bytes changed');
   563	
   564	  const primaryIds = manifest.primaryCohorts.map((cohort) => cohort.id);
   565	  addViolation(violations, manifest.primaryCohorts.length === 2 && new Set(primaryIds).size === 2,
   566	    'primary_cohort_set', 'manifest must contain one hard and one brutal primary cohort');
   567	  const allSeeds = new Set<number>();
   568	  for (const difficulty of ['hard', 'brutal'] as const) {
   569	    const cohort = manifest.primaryCohorts.find((candidate) => candidate.difficulty === difficulty);
   570	    if (cohort === undefined) continue;
   571	    const expectedSeeds = expectedPrimarySeeds(difficulty);
   572	    addViolation(violations, canonicalEqual(cohort.fixtures.map((fixture) => fixture.seed), expectedSeeds),
   573	      'primary_seed_range', `${difficulty} primary cohort has the wrong seeds`);
   574	    for (const [index, fixture] of cohort.fixtures.entries()) {
   575	      const expectedSeed = expectedSeeds[index];
   576	      addViolation(violations, fixture.path ===
   577	        `${expectedPrimaryDirectory(difficulty)}/seed-${String(fixture.seed)}.json`,
   578	      'primary_fixture_path', `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} has a noncanonical path`);
   579	      addViolation(violations, !allSeeds.has(fixture.seed), 'duplicate_seed',
   580	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} appears more than once`);
   581	      allSeeds.add(fixture.seed);
   582	      if (fixture.seed !== expectedSeed) continue;
   583	      try {
   584	        const bytes = access.readText(fixture.path);
   585	        addViolation(violations, sha256(bytes) === fixture.sha256, 'primary_fixture_hash',
   586	          `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} fixture hash changed`);
   587	        const parsed = JSON.parse(bytes) as { readonly spec?: {
   588	          readonly seed?: unknown; readonly difficultyProfile?: unknown;
   589	        } };
   590	        addViolation(violations, parsed.spec?.seed === fixture.seed &&
   591	          parsed.spec.difficultyProfile === difficulty, 'primary_fixture_identity',
   592	        `seed ${String(fixture.seed)} fixture identity or difficulty changed`);
   593	      } catch (error) {
   594	        violations.push({
   595	          code: 'primary_fixture_missing',
   596	          message: `${fixture.path}: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
   597	        });
   598	      }
   599	    }
   600	  }
   601	
   602	  try {
   603	    const secondBytes = access.readText(manifest.secondFamily.manifestPath);
   604	    addViolation(violations, sha256(secondBytes) === manifest.secondFamily.manifestSha256,
   605	      'second_family_manifest_hash', 'second-family manifest bytes changed');
   606	    const second = JSON.parse(secondBytes) as D569SecondFamilyManifest;
   607	    for (const violation of validateD569SecondFamilyManifest(second, access.secondFamilyAccess)) {
   608	      violations.push({ code: `second_family_${violation.code}`, message: violation.message });
   609	    }
   610	    const secondSeeds = second.cohorts.flatMap((cohort) => cohort.fixtures.map((fixture) => fixture.seed));
   611	    for (const seed of secondSeeds) {
   612	      addViolation(violations, !allSeeds.has(seed) && !manifest.trainingSeeds.includes(seed),
   613	        'second_family_overlap', `second-family seed ${String(seed)} is trained or overlaps evaluation`);
   614	    }
   615	    addViolation(violations,
   616	      canonicalEqual(second.cohorts.find((cohort) => cohort.difficulty === 'hard')?.fixtures
   617	        .map((fixture) => fixture.seed), D569_SECOND_FAMILY_SEEDS.hard) &&
   618	      canonicalEqual(second.cohorts.find((cohort) => cohort.difficulty === 'brutal')?.fixtures
   619	        .map((fixture) => fixture.seed), D569_SECOND_FAMILY_SEEDS.brutal),
   620	    'second_family_seed_range', 'fluke guard must use the frozen encounter cohort, not a shuffle seed');
   621	  } catch (error) {
   622	    violations.push({
   623	      code: 'second_family_manifest_missing',
   624	      message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
   625	    });
   626	  }
   627	  return violations;
   628	}

   630	export interface D569DryRunCell {
   631	  readonly arm: string;
   632	  readonly model: D569ExperimentArm['model'];
   633	  readonly effort: 'high';
   634	  readonly dmMode: 'blind' | 'advice';
   635	  readonly repair: 'code_only' | 'minimal_legal_alternative' | null;
   636	  readonly adviceAssisted: boolean;
   637	  readonly family: D569ExperimentFamily;
   638	  readonly basis: D569ExperimentBasis;
   639	  readonly seed: number;
   640	  readonly rep: 1 | 2 | 3;
   641	  readonly fixturePath: string;
   642	  readonly stateHash: string;
   643	  readonly sharedKbHash: string;
   644	  readonly visualSourceHash: string;
   645	  readonly visualProfileHash: string;
   646	  readonly sessionPolicy: 'fresh';
   647	  readonly sessionKey: string;
   648	  readonly timeoutMs: 240_000;
   649	  readonly escalation: false;
   650	  readonly modelDefaultFallback: false;
   651	  readonly baseContextCapBytes: number;
   652	  readonly semanticContextCapBytes: number;
   653	  readonly requiredBlocks: readonly ['semantic_board', 'creature_facts', 'initiative', 'legal_movement'];
   654	  readonly truncatedBlocks: readonly [];
   655	}
   656	
   657	function secondFamilyCohorts(
   658	  manifest: D569ExperimentManifest,
   659	  access: D569ExperimentValidationAccess,
   660	): D569ExperimentManifest['primaryCohorts'] {
   661	  const parsed = JSON.parse(access.readText(manifest.secondFamily.manifestPath)) as D569SecondFamilyManifest;
   662	  return parsed.cohorts.map((cohort) => ({
   663	    id: cohort.difficulty === 'hard' ? 'evaluation-hard' as const : 'evaluation-brutal' as const,
   664	    difficulty: cohort.difficulty,
   665	    fixtures: cohort.fixtures,
   666	  }));
   667	}
   668	
   669	/** Emits future execution cells only. This function has no process, arena, adapter, or model seam. */
   670	export function dryRunD569Experiment(
   671	  input: unknown,
   672	  access: D569ExperimentValidationAccess,
   673	  options: { readonly includeHintArms?: boolean; readonly family?: D569ExperimentFamily } = {},
   674	): readonly D569DryRunCell[] {
   675	  const violations = validateD569ExperimentManifest(input, access);
   676	  if (violations.length > 0) {
   677	    throw new TypeError(`Invalid D569 experiment manifest: ${violations[0]?.code ?? 'unknown'}`);
   678	  }
   679	  const manifest = d569ExperimentManifestSchema.parse(input);
   680	  const family = options.family ?? 'primary';
   681	  const cohorts = family === 'primary' ? manifest.primaryCohorts : secondFamilyCohorts(manifest, access);
   682	  const arms = options.includeHintArms === true
   683	    ? [...manifest.coreArms, ...manifest.hintArms]
   684	    : manifest.coreArms;
   685	  return arms.flatMap((arm) => cohorts.flatMap((cohort) => cohort.fixtures.flatMap((fixture) =>
   686	    ([1, 2, 3] as const).map((rep): D569DryRunCell => {
   687	      const visualPin = manifest.visualPins[arm.dmMode];
   688	      return {
   689	        arm: arm.id,
   690	        model: arm.model,
   691	        effort: arm.effort,
   692	        dmMode: arm.dmMode,
   693	        repair: arm.repair,
   694	        adviceAssisted: arm.adviceAssisted,
   695	        family,
   696	        basis: cohort.difficulty,
   697	        seed: fixture.seed,
   698	        rep,
   699	        fixturePath: fixture.path,
   700	        stateHash: fixture.sha256,
   701	        sharedKbHash: manifest.sharedKb.combinedStartupHash,
   702	        visualSourceHash: sha256(canonicalJson({ stateHash: fixture.sha256, role: visualPin.imageRole })),
   703	        visualProfileHash: sha256(canonicalJson(visualPin)),
   704	        sessionPolicy: 'fresh',
   705	        sessionKey: sha256(canonicalJson({ family, arm: arm.id, seed: fixture.seed, rep })),
   706	        timeoutMs: manifest.experimentWallMs,
   707	        escalation: false,
   708	        modelDefaultFallback: false,
   709	        baseContextCapBytes: arm.dmMode === 'blind'
   710	          ? manifest.caps.blindBaseBytes
   711	          : manifest.caps.adviceBaseBytes,
   712	        semanticContextCapBytes: SEMANTIC_BOARD_MAX_BYTES,
   713	        requiredBlocks: ['semantic_board', 'creature_facts', 'initiative', 'legal_movement'],
   714	        truncatedBlocks: [],
   715	      };
   716	    }))));
   717	}

   241	    ...auditEncounterState(input.state),
   242	  }));
   243	  const familyCounts = (['hard', 'brutal', 'brutal-b', 'pool'] as const).map((family) => [
   244	    family,
   245	    rooms.filter((row) => row.family === family).reduce<EraAuditCounts>(addCounts, emptyCounts()),
   246	  ] as const);
   247	  const families = Object.fromEntries(familyCounts) as Readonly<Record<EraAuditFamily, EraAuditCounts>>;
   248	  return {
   249	    script_version: LOS_COVER_ERA_AUDIT_VERSION,
   250	    engine_revision: LOS_COVER_ENGINE_REVISION,
   251	    terrain_profiles: Object.fromEntries(TERRAIN_KINDS.map((kind) => [kind, {
   252	      cover_tier: TERRAIN_PROFILES[kind].coverTier,
   253	      passability: TERRAIN_PROFILES[kind].passability,
   254	      blocks_sight: TERRAIN_PROFILES[kind].blocksSight,
   255	    }])) as EraAuditReport['terrain_profiles'],
   256	    rooms,
   257	    families,
   258	    overall: rooms.reduce<EraAuditCounts>(addCounts, emptyCounts()),
   259	  };

   262	async function fixtureRoom(family: Exclude<EraAuditFamily, 'pool'>, seed: number): Promise<{ readonly state: EncounterState; readonly bytes: string }> {
   263	  const path = resolve(`tests/fixtures/arena-basis-${family}/seed-${String(seed)}.json`);
   264	  const bytes = await readFile(path, 'utf8');
   265	  return { state: decodeArenaFixtureText(bytes), bytes };
   266	}
   267	
   268	export async function buildEraAuditReport(): Promise<EraAuditReport> {
   269	  const definitions = [
   270	    ['hard', HARD_SEEDS],
   271	    ['brutal', BRUTAL_SEEDS],
   272	    ['brutal-b', BRUTAL_B_SEEDS],
   273	    ['pool', POOL_SEEDS],
   274	  ] as const;
   275	  const inputs: EraAuditRoomInput[] = [];
   276	  for (const [family, seeds] of definitions) {
   277	    for (const [index, seed] of seeds.entries()) {
   278	      const loaded = family === 'pool'
   279	        ? (() => {
   280	            const room = generateRoom(seed, { difficulty: 'brutal' });
   281	            const bytes = `${canonicalJson(room)}\n`;
   282	            return { state: room.encounter.state, bytes };
   283	          })()
   284	        : await fixtureRoom(family, seed);
   285	      inputs.push({
   286	        family,
   287	        seed,
   288	        room: index + 1,
   289	        fixtureHash: sha256(loaded.bytes),
   290	        state: loaded.state,
   291	      });
   292	    }
   293	  }
   294	  if (inputs.length !== ERA_AUDIT_ROOM_COUNT) throw new Error(`Era audit expected 63 rooms, received ${String(inputs.length)}.`);
   295	  return buildEraAuditReportFromRooms(inputs);
   296	}

   118	type RoundExecutionResult =
   119	  | { readonly seed: number; readonly outcome: 'executed'; readonly state: EncounterState }
   120	  | {
   121	      readonly seed: number;
   122	      readonly outcome: 'execution_failed';

   126	
   127	function livingMonsterIds(state: EncounterState): readonly CombatantId[] {
   128	  return state.combatants.flatMap((combatant) =>
   129	    combatant.profile.kind === 'monster' && combatant.life === 'living'
   130	      ? [combatant.profile.id]
   131	      : []);
   132	}
   133	
   134	function maximalMonsterSegment(state: EncounterState): readonly CombatantId[] {
   135	  if (state.activeInitiativeIndex === null) return [];
   136	  const actors: CombatantId[] = [];
   137	  for (let index = state.activeInitiativeIndex; index < state.initiative.length; index += 1) {
   138	    const initiative = state.initiative[index];
   139	    if (initiative === undefined) throw new Error('Execution invariant encountered a missing initiative entry.');
   140	    const combatant = state.combatants.find((candidate) => candidate.profile.id === initiative.combatant);
   141	    if (combatant === undefined) throw new Error(`Execution invariant cannot find ${initiative.combatant}.`);
   142	    if (combatant.life === 'dead') continue;
   143	    if (combatant.profile.kind === 'player_character') break;
   144	    actors.push(combatant.profile.id);
   145	  }
   146	  return actors;
   147	}
   148	
   149	function deterministicActivationChoice(option: EngineOfferableOption): EngineActivationChoice | undefined {
   150	  const slot = option.activationChoice;
   151	  if (slot === undefined || slot === null) return undefined;
   152	  switch (slot.kind) {
   153	    case 'command_word': return { kind: slot.kind, value: slot.values[0] };
   154	    case 'unicorns_blessing_spell': return { kind: slot.kind, value: slot.values[0] };
   155	    case 'dispel_evil_and_good_mode': return { kind: slot.kind, value: slot.values[0] };
   156	    case 'calm_emotions_per_target': return {
   157	      kind: slot.kind,
   158	      selections: slot.targetIds.map((targetId) => ({ targetId, mode: slot.values[0] })),
   159	    };
   160	  }
   161	}
   162	
   163	function dryRunMonsterPlan(state: EncounterState): ReadonlyMap<CombatantId, AuthorizedEngineTurnProposal> {
   164	  const actorIds = [...livingMonsterIds(state)].sort((left, right) => left.localeCompare(right));
   165	  const planningState = projectFutureMonsterTurns(state, actorIds);
   166	  return new Map(actorIds.map((actorId) => {
   167	    const report = actorOpportunityReport(
   168	      planningState,
   169	      actorId,
   170	      OFFER_ENVIRONMENT,
   171	      state.revision,
   172	    );
   173	    const primary = report.defaultOption;
   174	    const fallback = availableEngineActorOptions(
   175	      planningState,
   176	      actorId,
   177	      OFFER_ENVIRONMENT,
   178	      state.revision,
   179	    ).find((option) => option.optionId !== primary.optionId);
   180	    if (fallback === undefined) throw new Error(`Dry-run plan has no independent fallback for ${actorId}.`);
   181	    const activationChoice = deterministicActivationChoice(primary);
   182	    const proposal: EngineTurnProposal = {
   183	      actorId,
   184	      expectedRevision: state.revision,
   185	      primaryOptionId: primary.optionId,
   186	      fallbackOptionId: fallback.optionId,
   187	      reason: 'Use the engine-ranked option to maximize immediate tactical value.',
   188	      ...(activationChoice === undefined ? {} : { activationChoice }),
   189	      overrideJustification: null,
   190	    };
   191	    const resolution = TURN_PROPOSAL_RESOLVER.resolve(planningState, proposal);
   192	    if (!resolution.valid) {
   193	      throw new Error(`Dry-run plan was refused for ${actorId}: ${resolution.refusals.map((entry) => entry.code).join(', ')}.`);
   194	    }
   195	    return [actorId, {
   196	      proposal,
   197	      option: resolution.option,
   198	      primaryOption: resolution.primaryOption,
   199	      fallbackOption: resolution.fallbackOption,
   200	      mechanics: resolution.mechanics,
   201	      selectedBranch: resolution.selectedBranch,
   202	    }] as const;
   203	  }));
   204	}
   205	
   206	function executeFrozenRound(
   207	  room: GeneratedRoom,
   208	  policy: ReactionOfferHostPolicy = { kind: 'unattended', askDefault: 'decline' },
   209	): RoundExecutionResult {
   210	  const seed = room.spec.seed;
   211	  const session = new EngineRoundSession(
   212	    applyRoomInitiativeProfile(decodeArenaFixture(room), 'derived_v1'),
   213	    mulberry32(8_274_113),
   214	    policy,
   215	    OFFER_ENVIRONMENT,
   216	  );
   217	  try {
   218	    session.beginRoundWithoutSkipping({
   219	      runId: encounterSessionId(`encounter:arena-execution-invariant:${String(seed)}`),
   220	      branchId: encounterBranchId(`branch:arena-execution-invariant:${String(seed)}`),
   221	      revision: 1,
   222	      requestId: `request:arena-execution-invariant:${String(seed)}`,
   223	      phase: 'initial',
   224	      room: 1,
   225	      historyKind: 'room_ready',
   226	    }, null);
   227	    const roundStart = session.currentState();
   228	    const round = roundStart.round;
   229	    const partyPlan = createScriptedPartyPlan(roundStart, {
   230	      decisionPolicy: DEFAULT_SCRIPTED_PARTY_DECISION_POLICY,
   231	    });
   232	    const monsterPlan = dryRunMonsterPlan(roundStart);
   233	    const acted = new Set<CombatantId>();
   234	    for (let step = 0; step <= roundStart.initiative.length; step += 1) {
   235	      const state = session.currentState();
   236	      if (state.phase.kind === 'concluded' || state.round > round) {
   237	        return { seed, outcome: 'executed', state };
   238	      }
   239	      if (state.activeCombatant === null) throw new Error('Round execution lost its active combatant.');
   240	      if (acted.has(state.activeCombatant)) {
   241	        throw new Error(state.pendingDecisions.length > 0
   242	          ? 'Round execution reached an already-acted actor with unresolved pending decisions.'
   243	          : 'Round execution stalled on an already-acted actor before advancing the round.');
   244	      }
   245	      const active = state.combatants.find((combatant) =>
   246	        combatant.profile.id === state.activeCombatant);
   247	      if (active === undefined) throw new Error(`Execution invariant cannot find ${state.activeCombatant}.`);
   248	      if (active.profile.kind === 'player_character') {
   249	        session.completeScriptedPcTurn(materializeScriptedPartyTurn({
   250	          state,
   251	          plan: partyPlan,
   252	          actorId: active.profile.id,
   253	        }), null);
   254	        acted.add(active.profile.id);
   255	        continue;
   256	      }
   257	      const segment = maximalMonsterSegment(state);
   258	      const applications = segment.map((actorId) => {
   259	        const application = monsterPlan.get(actorId);
   260	        if (application === undefined) throw new Error(`Dry-run plan omitted ${actorId}.`);
   261	        acted.add(actorId);
   262	        return application;
   263	      });
   264	      session.applyConsecutiveMonsterSegment(applications, null);
   265	    }
   266	    throw new Error(`Round ${String(round)} did not complete within one initiative cycle.`);
   267	  } catch (error) {
   268	    return {
   269	      seed,
   270	      outcome: 'execution_failed',
   271	      error: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
   272	      state: session.currentState(),
   273	    };
   274	  }
   275	}
   276	
   277	function assertRoundsExecuted(results: readonly RoundExecutionResult[]): void {
   278	  const failure = results.find((result) => result.outcome === 'execution_failed');
   279	  if (failure !== undefined) {
   280	    throw new Error(`Seed ${String(failure.seed)} failed round execution: ${failure.error}`);
   281	  }
   282	}
   283	
   284	function cellIsInBounds(
   285	  cell: { readonly column: number; readonly row: number },
   286	  bounds: { readonly columns: number; readonly rows: number },
   287	): boolean {
   288	  return cell.column >= 0 && cell.column < bounds.columns &&

   173	function independentMulberry32(seed: number): () => number {
   174	  let state = seed >>> 0;
   175	  return () => {
   176	    state = (state + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
   177	    let mixed = state;
   178	    mixed = Math.imul(mixed ^ (mixed >>> 15), mixed | 1);
   179	    mixed ^= mixed + Math.imul(mixed ^ (mixed >>> 7), mixed | 61);
   180	    return ((mixed ^ (mixed >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4_294_967_296;
   181	  };
   182	}

    90	function requiredValue(argv: readonly string[], index: number, option: string): string {

   104	function parseOptions(argv: readonly string[]): {
   105	  readonly flags: ReadonlySet<string>;
   106	  readonly values: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
   107	} {
   108	  const args = argv[0] === '--' ? argv.slice(1) : argv;
   109	  const flags = new Set<string>();
   110	  const values = new Map<string, string>();
   111	  const knownFlags = new Set(['--verify-only']);
   112	  const knownValues = new Set([
   113	    '--difficulty', '--seed', '--rooms', '--out', '--terrain-profile', '--protocol',
   114	    '--party-pack-dir', '--manifest', '--basis-dir', '--basis-manifest',
   115	    '--manifest-sha256', '--expect-rooms',
   116	  ]);
   117	  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {
   118	    const option = args[index];
   119	    if (option === undefined) throw new TypeError('Basis-generator option is missing.');
   120	    if (knownFlags.has(option)) {
   121	      flags.add(option);
   122	      continue;
   123	    }
   124	    if (!knownValues.has(option)) throw new TypeError(`Unknown basis-generator option ${option}.`);
   125	    values.set(option, requiredValue(args, index, option));
   126	    index += 1;
   127	  }
   128	  return { flags, values };
   129	}

   147	    throw new TypeError(`Options are not valid for this basis mode: ${unexpected.join(', ')}.`);

   163	    const manifestSha256 = parsed.values.get('--manifest-sha256');

   165	      throw new TypeError('--verify-only requires --basis-dir, --basis-manifest, and --manifest-sha256.');

   173	      expectRooms: safeInteger(parsed.values.get('--expect-rooms') ?? '', '--expect-rooms', 1),

   175	  }
   176	  if (protocol !== null) {

   179	    ]), new Set());
   180	    const out = parsed.values.get('--out');

   185	    }

   187	      protocol,

   190	      partyPackPath: resolve(partyPackPath),
   191	      outPath: resolve(out),
   192	      manifestPath: resolve(manifestPath),
   193	    };
   194	  }
   195	  if (parsed.values.has('--protocol')) {

   197	  }

   222	export function heldoutBasisSchedule(protocol: HeldoutOrdinaryProtocol, ordinal: number) {
   223	  const localOrdinal = ordinal % 24;
   224	  const level = (3 + localOrdinal % 4) as HeldoutPartyLevel;
   225	  const targetXp: Readonly<Record<HeldoutPartyLevel, HeldoutTargetXp>> = {
   226	    3: 900, 4: 1_500, 5: 3_000, 6: 4_000,
   227	  };
   228	  const slices = ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F'] as const;
   229	  const partition: HeldoutPartition | undefined = protocol === 'heldout-development-v1'
   230	    ? 'development'
   231	    : slices[Math.floor(ordinal / 24)];
   232	  if (partition === undefined) throw new RangeError('Held-out reserve supports six 24-room slices.');
   233	  return {
   234	    partition,
   235	    level,
   236	    targetXp: targetXp[level],
   237	    terrainProfile: Math.floor(localOrdinal / 4) % 2 === 0
   238	      ? 'los_cover_v1' as const
   239	      : null,
   240	  };
   241	}

function evaluateScenarioFact(
  state: Parameters<typeof evaluateScenarioFactWithQueries>[0],
  fact: Parameters<typeof evaluateScenarioFactWithQueries>[1],
): ReturnType<typeof evaluateScenarioFactWithQueries> {
  return evaluateScenarioFactWithQueries(state, fact, OFFER_ENVIRONMENT.queries);
}

function evaluateHostScenarios(
  state: Parameters<typeof evaluateHostScenariosWithEnvironment>[0],
  scenarios: Parameters<typeof evaluateHostScenariosWithEnvironment>[1],
): ReturnType<typeof evaluateHostScenariosWithEnvironment> {
  return evaluateHostScenariosWithEnvironment(state, scenarios, OFFER_ENVIRONMENT.queries);
}

const HARD_BASIS_SEEDS = [
  5_117_001, 5_117_002, 5_117_003, 5_117_004, 5_117_005, 5_117_006,
  5_117_007, 5_117_008, 5_117_009, 5_117_010, 5_117_011, 5_117_012,
] as const;

const hardBasisInputs = declareTestInputs({
  fixtures: HARD_BASIS_SEEDS.map((seed): `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-hard/seed-${number}.json` =>
    `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-hard/seed-${seed}.json`),
});

function frozenHardState(seed: (typeof HARD_BASIS_SEEDS)[number]): EncounterState {
  const path: `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-hard/seed-${number}.json` =
    `tests/fixtures/arena-basis-hard/seed-${seed}.json`;
  return decodeArenaFixtureText(hardBasisInputs.fixtures.readText(path));
}

function direct(actorId: ReturnType<typeof combatantId>): EngineSelectorRef {
  return { actorId, selector: { kind: 'combatant', combatantId: actorId } };
}

function compactState(): {
  readonly state: EncounterState;
  readonly source: ReturnType<typeof playerProfile>;
  readonly target: ReturnType<typeof monsterProfile>;
} {
  const source = playerProfile('spec-source', {
    hitPoints: 20,
    initiativeBonus: 20,
    spellSlots: [{ level: 3, maximum: 2 }],
  });
  const target = monsterProfile('spec-target', { hitPoints: 40, initiativeBonus: 0 });
  const initial = createEncounter({
    bounds: { columns: 8, rows: 4 },
    combatants: [source, target],
    tokens: [placedToken(source, 1, 1), placedToken(target, 5, 1)],
  });
  return {
    state: reduceEncounter(initial, { type: 'roll_initiative' }, () => 0.5).state,
    source,
    target,
  };
}

   599	}

   601	export function computeHostSplitCandidates(
   602	  state: EncounterState,
   603	  dependencies: readonly ProposalFactDependency[],
   604	  unactedPlayerIds: readonly CombatantId[],
   605	  queries: EngineQueryPort,
   606	): readonly HostSplitCandidate[] {
   607	  const grouped = new Map<string, {
   608	    readonly baseline: ScenarioFactAtom;
   609	    readonly flipped: ScenarioFactAtom;
   610	    readonly proposalActorIds: Set<CombatantId>;
   611	  }>();
   612	  const canonicalPlayerIds = [...new Set(unactedPlayerIds)].sort(compareCanonicalBytes);
   613	  for (const dependency of dependencies) {
   614	    const key = scenarioFactKey(dependency.baseline);
   615	    if (!scenarioFactsAreComplements(dependency.baseline, dependency.flipped) ||
   616	      !candidateAdvertised(state, dependency.baseline, queries)) continue;
   617	    const prior = grouped.get(key);
   618	    if (prior === undefined) {
   619	      grouped.set(key, {
   620	        baseline: dependency.baseline,
   621	        flipped: dependency.flipped,
   622	        proposalActorIds: new Set([dependency.proposalActorId]),
   623	      });
   624	    } else if (canonicalJson(prior.baseline) === canonicalJson(dependency.baseline) &&
   625	      canonicalJson(prior.flipped) === canonicalJson(dependency.flipped)) {
   626	      prior.proposalActorIds.add(dependency.proposalActorId);
   627	    }
   628	  }
   629	  const scored = [...grouped.entries()].flatMap(([factKey, dependency]) => {
   630	    const influences = canonicalPlayerIds
   631	      .flatMap((playerId) => {
   632	        const radius = maximumInfluenceRadiusFeet(state, playerId);
   633	        const canFlip = canPlayerFlipScenarioFact(state, playerId, dependency.flipped, queries);
   634	        return radius > 0 && canFlip
   635	          ? [{ playerId, radius }]
   636	          : [];
   637	      });
   638	    const referencedProposalCount = dependency.proposalActorIds.size;
   639	    const summedMovementRadiusFeet = influences.reduce((sum, entry) => sum + entry.radius, 0);
   640	    const volatilityScore = referencedProposalCount * summedMovementRadiusFeet;
   641	    return volatilityScore === 0 ? [] : [{
   642	      factKey,
   643	      baseline: dependency.baseline,
   644	      flipped: dependency.flipped,
   645	      referencedProposalCount,
   646	      influencingPlayerIds: influences.map((entry) => entry.playerId),
   647	      summedMovementRadiusFeet,
   648	      volatilityScore,
   649	    }];
   650	  });
   651	  scored.sort((left, right) =>
   652	    right.volatilityScore - left.volatilityScore ||
   653	    right.referencedProposalCount - left.referencedProposalCount ||
   654	    compareCanonicalBytes(left.factKey, right.factKey));
   655	  const retained: typeof scored = [];
   656	  for (const candidate of scored) {
   657	    if (retained.some((higher) => shadowedBy(higher.baseline, candidate.baseline))) continue;
   658	    retained.push(candidate);
   659	  }
   660	  return retained.slice(0, 8).map((candidate, index) => ({
   661	    ...candidate,
   662	    candidateId: `candidate:${sha256(canonicalJson({
   663	      factKey: candidate.factKey,
   664	      baseline: candidate.baseline,
   665	      flipped: candidate.flipped,
   666	    })).slice(0, 32)}`,
   667	    rank: (index + 1) as HostSplitCandidate['rank'],
   668	  }));
   669	}

   671	export function buildHostScenarioMenu(
   672	  state: EncounterState,
   673	  actors: readonly CombatantId[],
   674	  unactedPlayerIds: readonly CombatantId[],
   675	  environment: EngineOptionEnvironment,
   676	): {
   677	  readonly baselineProposals: readonly EngineTurnProposal[];
   678	  readonly scenarioMenu: readonly HostSplitCandidate[];
   679	  readonly scenarios: readonly HostScenario[];
   680	} {
   681	  const queries = environment.queries;
   682	  const planningState = projectFutureMonsterTurns(state, actors);
   683	  const baselineProposals = hostBaselineProposalPlanner.plan(planningState, actors, environment);
   684	  const baselineOptions = baselineProposals.flatMap((proposal) =>
   685	    availableEngineActorOptions(planningState, proposal.actorId, environment).filter((option) =>
   686	      option.optionId === proposal.primaryOptionId));
   687	  const scenarioMenu = computeHostSplitCandidates(
   688	    state,
   689	    extractProposalFactDependencies(state, baselineOptions, queries),
   690	    unactedPlayerIds,
   691	    queries,
   692	  );
   693	  return { baselineProposals, scenarioMenu, scenarios: compileHostScenarios(scenarioMenu) };
   694	}
   695	
   696	export function compileHostScenarios(
   697	  menu: readonly HostSplitCandidate[],
   698	): readonly HostScenario[] {
   699	  if (menu.length === 0) return [];
   700	  if (menu.length > 8) throw new RangeError('A host scenario menu contains at most eight candidates.');
   701	  const ordered = [...menu].sort((left, right) => left.rank - right.rank);
   702	  if (ordered.some((candidate, index) => candidate.rank !== index + 1)) {
   703	    throw new RangeError('Host split-candidate ranks must be contiguous and canonical.');
   704	  }
   705	  const selected = ordered.slice(0, 3);
   706	  if (new Set(selected.map((candidate) => candidate.factKey)).size !== selected.length ||
   707	    selected.some((candidate) => !scenarioFactsAreComplements(candidate.baseline, candidate.flipped))) {
   708	    throw new RangeError('Host scenarios require unique fact keys and exact complements.');
   709	  }
   710	  const scenarioSetKey = selected.map((candidate) => candidate.candidateId);
   711	  return selected.map((_candidate, index) => {
   712	    const ordinal = (index + 2) as HostScenario['ordinal'];
   713	    return {
   714	      scenarioId: `scenario:${sha256(canonicalJson({ scenarioSetKey, ordinal })).slice(0, 32)}`,
   715	      ordinal,
   716	      kind: 'single_candidate_flip' as const,
   717	      flippedCandidateId: selected[index]?.candidateId ?? null,
   718	      facts: selected.map((candidate, factIndex) =>
   719	        factIndex === index ? candidate.flipped : candidate.baseline),
   720	    };
   721	  }).reduce<HostScenario[]>((scenarios, scenario) => {
   722	    if (scenarios.length === 0) {
   723	      scenarios.push({
   724	        scenarioId: `scenario:${sha256(canonicalJson({ scenarioSetKey, ordinal: 1 })).slice(0, 32)}`,
   725	        ordinal: 1,
   726	        kind: 'no_material_change',
   727	        flippedCandidateId: null,
   728	        facts: selected.map((candidate) => candidate.baseline),
   729	      });
   730	    }
   731	    scenarios.push(scenario);
   732	    return scenarios;
   733	  }, []);
   734	}

  1209	export function blindSemanticBoard(
  1210	  projection: EngineSemanticBoardProjection,
  1211	  stateDigest: string,
  1212	): BlindSemanticBoard {
  1213	  const payload: SemanticBoardPayload = semanticBoardPayload(projection);
  1214	  if (payload.audience !== 'dm') throw new TypeError('Blind semantic board must have DM audience.');
  1215	  const { reach_range_summaries: _reachRangeSummaries, ...retained } = payload;
  1216	  const candidate = {
  1217	    provenance: {
  1218	      kind: 'engine_fact',
  1219	      format: SEMANTIC_BOARD_FORMAT,
  1220	      state_digest: stateDigest,
  1221	    },
  1222	    ...retained,
  1223	    audience: 'dm',
  1224	  };
  1225	  return blindSemanticBoardSchema.parse(candidate);
  1226	}

   100	/** Total, side-effect-free evaluation against the actual canonical encounter state. */
   101	export function evaluateScenarioFact(
   102	  state: EncounterState,
   103	  atom: ScenarioFactAtom,
   104	  queries: EngineQueryPort,
   105	): GuardAtomEvaluation {
   106	  switch (atom.kind) {
   107	    case 'life_state_is': {
   108	      const subjectId = resolveSelector(state, atom.subject, queries);
   109	      if (subjectId === null) return failure('SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED');
   110	      return compared(queries.combatant(state, subjectId)?.life ?? null, atom.value);
   111	    }
   112	    case 'hp_percent': {
   113	      const subjectId = resolveSelector(state, atom.subject, queries);
   114	      if (subjectId === null) return failure('SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED');
   115	      const subject = queries.combatant(state, subjectId);
   116	      if (subject?.life !== 'living') return failure('SUBJECT_NOT_LIVING');
   117	      const maximum = enginePlanningHitPointMaximum(state, subjectId);
   118	      if (!Number.isFinite(maximum) || maximum <= 0) return failure('HP_MAXIMUM_UNAVAILABLE');
   119	      const current = enginePlanningHitPoints(state, subjectId);
   120	      const actual = atom.comparison === 'at_most'
   121	        ? current * 100 <= maximum * atom.threshold
   122	        : current * 100 > maximum * atom.threshold;
   123	      return compared(actual, true);
   124	    }
   125	    case 'adjacency_is': {
   126	      const subjects = pair(state, atom.left, atom.right, queries);
   127	      if (isEvaluation(subjects)) return subjects;
   128	      const separation = queries.spaceDistance(state, subjects.left, subjects.right);
   129	      if (separation === null) return failure('TOKEN_UNAVAILABLE');
   130	      return compared(separation <= 5, atom.value);
   131	    }
   132	    case 'within_action_reach_is': {
   133	      const subjects = pair(state, atom.actor, atom.target, queries);
   134	      if (isEvaluation(subjects)) return subjects;
   135	      if (!queries.actions(state, subjects.left).some((action) => action.id === atom.actionId)) {
   136	        return failure('ACTION_UNAVAILABLE');
   137	      }
   138	      const reach = queries.reach(state, {
   139	        actorId: subjects.left,
   140	        targetId: subjects.right,
   141	        actionId: atom.actionId,
   142	      });
   143	      if (!reach.legal && reach.codes.some((code) => code !== 'target_out_of_range')) {
   144	        return failure('ACTION_UNAVAILABLE');
   145	      }
   146	      return compared(reach.legal, atom.value);
   147	    }
   148	    case 'visibility_is': {
   149	      const subjects = pair(state, atom.observer, atom.subject, queries);
   150	      if (isEvaluation(subjects)) return subjects;
   151	      const visibility = queries.visibility(state, subjects.left, subjects.right);
   152	      if (visibility === null) return failure('VISIBILITY_UNAVAILABLE');
   153	      return compared(visibility.visible, atom.value);
   154	    }
   155	    case 'zone_occupancy_is': {
   156	      const subjectId = resolveSelector(state, atom.subject, queries);
   157	      if (subjectId === null) return failure('SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED');
   158	      const zone = enginePlanningSemanticZones(state).find((candidate) => candidate.id === atom.zoneId);
   159	      if (zone === undefined || !zone.active) return failure('ZONE_UNAVAILABLE');
   160	      const actual = zone.memberCombatantIds.includes(subjectId) ? 'inside' : 'outside';
   161	      return compared(actual, atom.value);
   162	    }
   163	    case 'condition_is': {
   164	      const subjectId = resolveSelector(state, atom.subject, queries);
   165	      if (subjectId === null) return failure('SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED');
   166	      const present = combatantConditions(state, subjectId).some((condition) =>
   167	        sameCondition(condition, atom.condition));
   168	      return compared(present, atom.present);
   169	    }
   170	    case 'resource_available_is': {
   171	      const subjectId = resolveSelector(state, atom.subject, queries);
   172	      if (subjectId === null) return failure('SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED');
   173	      const subject = queries.combatant(state, subjectId);
   174	      if (subject === null) return failure('SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED');
   175	      let available: boolean;
   176	      switch (atom.resource.kind) {
   177	        case 'reaction': available = subject.turn.reactionAvailable === true; break;
   178	        case 'legendary_action': {
   179	          if (subject.legendary === undefined) return failure('RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE');
   180	          available = subject.legendary.actionUsesRemaining > 0;
   181	          break;
   182	        }
   183	        case 'legendary_resistance': {
   184	          if (subject.legendary === undefined) return failure('RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE');
   185	          available = subject.legendary.resistanceUsesRemaining > 0;
   186	          break;
   187	        }
   188	        case 'spell_slot': {
   189	          const level = atom.resource.level;
   190	          const slot = subject.spellSlots.find((candidate) => candidate.level === level);
   191	          if (slot === undefined) return failure('RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE');
   192	          available = slot.remaining > 0;
   193	          break;
   194	        }
   195	      }
   196	      return compared(available, atom.available);
   197	    }
   198	    case 'concentration_is': {
   199	      const subjectId = resolveSelector(state, atom.subject, queries);
   200	      if (subjectId === null) return failure('SELECTOR_UNRESOLVED');
   201	      return compared(engineConcentrationActive(state, subjectId), atom.active);
   202	    }
   203	  }
   204	}

   210	function compareCanonicalBytes(left: string, right: string): number {
   211	  const leftBytes = new TextEncoder().encode(left);
   212	  const rightBytes = new TextEncoder().encode(right);
   213	  const sharedLength = Math.min(leftBytes.length, rightBytes.length);
   214	  for (let index = 0; index < sharedLength; index += 1) {
   215	    const leftByte = leftBytes[index];
   216	    const rightByte = rightBytes[index];
   217	    if (leftByte === undefined || rightByte === undefined) break;
   218	    if (leftByte !== rightByte) return leftByte - rightByte;
   219	  }
   220	  return leftBytes.length - rightBytes.length;
   220	  return leftBytes.length - rightBytes.length;
   221	}
